body.x: UNIUNI Corp (CEO Sooyeon Han) announced that it achieved over 30 billion KRW in cumulative export consultation results with its restroom safety and security solution, Savvy, at CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and tech exhibition held in Las Vegas early last month.
UNIUNI is a deep-tech startup that has developed and commercialized spatial safety solutions that do not raise privacy concerns through AI.

The industry recognizes the differentiation of UNIUNI’s real-time observation and detection solutions, which are designed using non-video technology that does not rely on direct video or image capture. The company explains that it helps resolve safety issues in public facilities by detecting falls, abnormal behavior, and emergencies in the observation area with high accuracy, and by delivering alerts to managers to enable rapid responses.

Savvy, the representative solution reflecting this technological prowess, is being distributed primarily to commercial, domestic, and public facilities, and reports indicate that it has been introduced to more than 127 facilities as of the end of last year. Furthermore, the company is expanding its overseas references by exporting to Japan, Malaysia, Switzerland, and other countries. It expects to achieve results by pioneering new sales channels based on the global market interest generated at CES 2026.

While Human Security for All has been a significant theme at CES since 2024, Savvy is widely regarded as a potent security solution that delivers on that value. This is because it recognizes various behavior types that threaten safety within a specific space, using 3D ToF (Time-of-Flight) sensors instead of cameras, ensuring it does not collect data directly linked to privacy, such as video or audio.

body.cap: RestroomGuard Savvy | Image provided by UNIUNI

body.x: In addition, the edge AI system, which does not rely on servers or networks, enables immediate responses, making it particularly useful in facilities where sensitive information is dispersed, including restrooms, nursing homes, hospitals, and clinics. Furthermore, Savvy earned recognition for its high scalability across numerous public facilities and smart cities, winning Innovation Awards in two categories at CES 2026: Human Security and Smart Cities.

By simultaneously securing two Innovation Awards and winning for the second consecutive year, UNIUNI attracted a total of 59 export consultations at the CES 2026 site. The cumulative consultation value resulting from this reaches 20.64 million USD (approximately 30.165 billion KRW).

A UNIUNI official expressed their feelings, stating, “We feel pleased that UNIUNI’s challenge to connect the value of advanced technology with human safety received high recognition on the global stage of CES 2026.”

They continued, “We gained significant interest, particularly from decision-makers in the public facility and smart city sectors who must consider both personal information protection and safety, and we will initiate entry into new markets using the network secured here as nourishment.” They emphasized, “Furthermore, by paralleling innovation in security technology, we will emerge as a global AI security leader protecting the safe daily lives of people worldwide.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
